angle: Instead of general backprop machinery, this video hand-computes the complete chain-rule derivative and every gradient-descent step for one single bias (b3, from 0 to 2.61) in a tiny drug-dosage network, so each symbol stays attached to a number.
angle_detail: Skim the forward-pass squiggle setup, then study [10:41]-[13:30] for the two-part chain-rule derivative and [13:38]-[16:03] for the learning-rate-0.1 iterations down to SSR 0.46 and below. Prerequisites from [00:19] are real: chain rule and gradient descent are assumed, not taught. Notation clash: sum of squared residuals (SSR) is the course's SSE/RSS idea, and only b3 is optimized while six parameters stay frozen.
